distinguishing_features: A passive solid high-permittivity stress-grade sleeve is physically installed at slot exits and terminations.
The mechanism changes local dielectric field distribution rather than measuring or predicting degradation.
It targets spike-event high-field nodes of the outermost turn and termination region.
It uses no sensors, telemetry, firmware, alarms, or trip logic.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce transient-overvoltage electric-field stress at vulnerable winding void/defect locations so partial discharge is avoided without adding bulk insulation or relying on monitoring.
parsed.viable_reason: The candidate computes the reduced field inside the high-ε solid, but PD occurs in the air void where the normal field is set by D/ε_void and would be unchanged or increased, so the stated mechanism does not suppress PD as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The distinguishing step is essentially a relocation of known stator end-winding stress-grade sleeves to other high-field winding sites, which a skilled engineer would routinely try for the same PD/corona field-grading problem.
